about.years.title: Where the years come from
about.years.lead: {with_year} buildings ({with_year_pct}) have a year. {record} come from a record: the Zagreb Building Stock Model (Zenodo) and the City of Zagreb's heritage registers (KULTURA_ZASTITA, KD_pojedinacna, OBNOVA_PROCELJA), and Wikidata or OpenStreetMap where they date a building. {area} take the year the City of Zagreb's heritage layer gives their whole area (its working data where nothing else dates them), and {estimated} are estimated. The other {unknown} have no year in any open source yet and are shown as “Year unknown”.
about.years.kinds: A year from a record is shown as the record gives it: an exact year ({exact} buildings), the year a building was finished when the record gives a span of up to fifteen years ({range}), or the first year of a longer span ({long}).
about.years.private: A private house shows only its decade, never its exact year: {private_dated} of the {private_cat} private houses have one. Its colour still shows its period, so where a period begins or ends within the decade, the colour narrows the decade to that part.

about.src.raa_old: An older register (years a newer record dropped)
about.src.raa_area: A record for a whole area (a block or an estate)
about.src.reader: A reader's report, checked by the map's maker
about.src.estimate: Estimated from similar dated buildings nearby
about.acc.title: How the estimates work, and how good they are
about.acc.how: For a house with no year, the map looks at the most similar dated buildings nearby (where they stand, how tall and how big they are, and what kind of building they are) and takes their typical year, the closest and most similar weighing most. To test this, every dated building was estimated as if it had no year, from the others, with whole city blocks left out together.
about.acc.rule: The map shows an estimated decade (“≈ 1950s”) only when all of these hold:
about.acc.rule.near: a dated building stands within {near} m;
about.acc.rule.late: it is not likely to be new: it was already in the City's 3D surveys before {late};
about.acc.rule.cell: its cell of the test has at least {min_cell} test buildings, puts at least {min_right} of them in the right period, and has a band of ±{max_band} years or less.
about.acc.result: {estimated} houses are estimated. In the test, {right} of the test houses in the cells the map uses were estimated in the right period ({right_n} of {n}), and {within} within one period. A cell's band is the range around the estimate that eight in ten true years fall inside.
about.acc.houses: The houses the map estimates, cell by cell:
about.acc.others: The other cells: houses the map does not estimate, and the other building types (the map estimates none of them)
about.acc.check: An independent check, on {check_n} buildings that only Wikidata or OpenStreetMap dates: the rule gave {check_shown} of them a decade, {check_right} in the right period. It is too small to confirm the test's figure.
about.acc.check.measured: An independent check, on {check_n} buildings that only Wikidata or OpenStreetMap dates: the rule gave {check_shown} of them a decade, {check_right} in the right period.
about.acc.check.new: It gave none of the {check_new} built from 1990 on a decade: a new building among older ones is the estimate's blind spot, and the rule keeps them off the map.
about.acc.area: Dating a building with its whole area was checked on {area_n} buildings that a record dates both ways: the area's year put {area_right} of them in the right period.
about.limits.title: What the map cannot tell you
about.limits.standing: Only buildings standing today. Demolished buildings are not on the map, so Play shows when today's buildings were built, not how fast the city grew.
about.limits.snapshot: A snapshot from {snapshot}. The City's 3D model is from then: buildings finished after it are missing.
about.limits.one: One year per building. Where a record gives a span of up to fifteen years, the map shows the year the building was finished; for a longer history it shows the first year, and the card gives the span.
about.limits.gamla: The old town (Gornji grad and Kaptol) is mostly “Year unknown”. Only {gamla_dated} of its {gamla_n} buildings have a year from a record, and the old town is not estimated, because the test shows it cannot be done well.
about.limits.new: New buildings are the estimate's blind spot: a new house among old ones would take its neighbours' age, so the map estimates no building the City first mapped in {late} or later.
about.limits.height: Heights are to the roof: spires and towers are not included. Floors come from OpenStreetMap where mapped ({floors_osm} buildings) and otherwise from the height (≈).
about.limits.colour: Colour shows the era, not the paint: a building's colour is its period, not the colour of its walls.
about.limits.private: Private houses show their decade only (see Privacy).
about.limits.terrain: The ground is drawn true to scale. The Hills slider under Look raises the hills up to {relief_max} times as high, or lays the city flat. The heights come from {terrain_from}.
about.limits.terrain.scaled: The ground is drawn {relief} times as high as it is. The Hills slider under Look sets it from flat up to {relief_max} times. The heights come from {terrain_from}.
about.privacy.title: Privacy
about.privacy.lead: This map is about buildings, not people.
about.privacy.shows: What the map shows. For every building on the map: its outline and height (City of Zagreb, ZG3D 2022), the year it was built and how we know it, and, where open sources have them, its name, architect and address.
about.privacy.never.who: Who owns or lives in a building: sentences in the Wikipedia texts that say so are left out.
about.privacy.never.ids: Cadastral parcel numbers or the registers' internal building and property ids.
about.privacy.never.byggherre: Who had a building built (the investor), except where the building's own name carries it, as many old names do.
about.privacy.never.year: The exact year of a private house.
about.privacy.private: Private houses. Private houses show only the decade they were built, for example “1950s”, never the exact year, and their cards do not link to the heritage register's record. An architect's name is left off a private house when it appears on {rare} or fewer buildings in the whole city, because on a family home a rare name may belong to the owner. Names of firms and housing cooperatives still show. Links to Wikipedia and Wikidata, Wikipedia texts and photos are left off private houses too, unless the house is one of the hand-checked landmarks.
about.privacy.private.address: A private house's street address is not shown on its card either, and search does not find it by its address.
about.privacy.why: Why we may show this. Everything comes from open public sources (see Sources). This is a non-commercial project that tells the story of how Zagreb was built, and it limits what it shows about private homes, as described above.
about.privacy.visit: Your visit. The map sets no cookies and runs no analytics or tracking script.
about.privacy.form: The report form. “Something wrong?” and “Suggest something” are not connected to a server yet, so nothing you type there is stored or sent. Until the map goes public, corrections go by email to the address under Contact.
about.privacy.hide: Hide a building, or correct it. If you own or live in a building and want its details taken off the map, or you have found a mistake, use “Something wrong?” on its card or write to {contact}. You do not need to say why. A hidden building keeps its shape, but its year, name, architect, address and links are removed in the next data update, as soon as we can and within the time the GDPR sets. You can also complain to the Croatian Personal Data Protection Agency (AZOP).
about.privacy.hide.nocontact: Hide a building, or correct it. If you own or live in a building and want its details taken off the map, or you have found a mistake, the address to write to is published under Contact before the map goes public. You will not need to say why. A hidden building keeps its shape, but its year, name, architect, address and links are removed in the next data update, as soon as we can and within the time the GDPR sets. You can also complain to the Croatian Personal Data Protection Agency (AZOP).
about.privacy.who: Who is responsible. Zagreb, building by building is a non-commercial pilot by {maker}, a port of Hus för hus (Stockholm).
about.privacy.who.nomaker: Who is responsible. Zagreb, building by building is a non-commercial pilot, a port of Hus för hus (Stockholm, MIT); its maker is named under Contact before the map goes public.
